where: Section 1, last bullet ("T is linear exactly when it sends every line...")
problem: The "exactly when" claim is false. A linear map does not keep the spacing of points on a line: T(v) = 2v doubles every distance, and it is linear. Also, "sends every line through the origin to a line through the origin" alone is not enough: T(x, y) = (x³, y³) sends each line through the origin to a line through the origin but is not linear. A student will read this as a usable test and mark wrong answers right.
fix: State it as a consequence, not a test: "A linear map sends each line through the origin to a line through the origin (or to {0}): T(tv) = t·T(v), so the image of the line spanned by v is the line spanned by T(v). The line may be stretched, shrunk or flattened, but it is never bent and it never moves off the origin."

where: Section 3, paragraph after the composition formula
problem: The justification labels do not match the steps shown. The first equality T(S(u + v)) = T(S(u) + S(v)) uses additivity of S, not just the definition, and the second equality T(S(u) + S(v)) = T(S(u)) + T(S(v)) uses additivity of T, not "linearity of S inside T". As written, a student cannot follow which map is doing the work.
fix: (T ∘ S)(u + v) = T(S(u + v)) [definition of ∘] = T(S(u) + S(v)) [additivity of S] = T(S(u)) + T(S(v)) [additivity of T] = (T ∘ S)(u) + (T ∘ S)(v) [definition of ∘]. The scaling line is the same: (T ∘ S)(cu) = T(c·S(u)) = c·T(S(u)).

where: Section 2, paragraph after the table ("Scaling by c stretches every length by |c| and fixes directions")
problem: "Fixes directions" is wrong for c < 0, where every direction is reversed, and "stretches" is wrong for |c| < 1, where lengths shrink. The same sentence then says the zero map (the case c = 0) crushes everything to 0, which contradicts "fixes directions".
fix: Scaling by c multiplies every length by |c| (a stretch when |c| > 1, a shrink when |c| < 1), keeps each direction when c > 0, reverses it when c < 0, and sends everything to 0 when c = 0.
